quiz.q: According to Maurice Duverger, what party system typically emerges from a simple majoritarian electoral system?
options: A two-party system, whereas proportional representation tends to produce a multi-party system.
A multi-party system, whereas proportional representation tends to produce a two-party system.
A one-party dominant system, because majoritarian rules suppress all competitive opposition parties.
A cadre-based party system, because majoritarian elections require highly centralized secret cells.
quiz.why: Duverger's Law states that simple majority single-ballot systems favor a two-party system, while proportional representation encourages multi-party systems.

quiz.q: According to Gabriel Almond's classification, which pressure groups are most prominent in developing countries?
options: Associational groups like formal trade unions and modern professional corporate lobbies.
Institutional groups like the military and bureaucracy, along with spontaneous anomic crowd protests.
Non-associational groups exclusively focused on global post-material and environmental developmental goals.
Pragmatic turnover groups operating primarily within institutionalized liberal two-party competitive systems.
quiz.why: Almond highlighted that developing states feature powerful institutional groups like civil servants and the army, alongside frequent anomic street protests.

quiz.q: How does Jean Blondel's dynamic model distinguish modern pressure groups from traditional ones?
options: Modern groups are community-based seeking protectionist benefits, while traditional groups have associational membership and developmental aims.
Modern groups rely on armed militia structures, while traditional groups operate exclusively through parliamentary branches and party cells.
Modern groups have associational membership pursuing developmental goals, while traditional groups are community-based and protectionist.
Modern groups function as secret vanguard societies, while traditional groups focus on pragmatic electoral turnover between parties.
quiz.why: Blondel explains that modernization shifts pressure groups from traditional community-based protectionist bodies to modern associational groups pursuing developmental goals.

quiz.q: How do social movements in developing countries like India differ from those in advanced Western nations?
options: Developing nations feature only post-materialist movements led and supported exclusively by industrial working-class laborers.
Developing nations rely solely on old movements using direct coercive strikes without addressing environmental or rights issues.
Developing nations lack social movements entirely because citizen participation is restricted strictly to formal institutional parties.
Developing nations witness a coexistence of old and new movements, combining material survival needs with post-material goals.
quiz.why: In developing countries, old materialist survival struggles coexist with new post-materialist issues, often combining a tribal base with middle-class leadership.
